==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|income}}, perhaps continuing (in altered form) {{inh|en|ang|incyme|t=an in-coming, entrance}}, equivalent to {{pre|en|in-|come}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Íenkúumen|t=income}}, {{cog|fy|ynkommen|t=income}}, {{cog|nl|inkomen}}, {{m|nl|inkomst|t=income, earnings, gainings}}, {{cog|nds-de|Inkumst|t=income}}, {{cog|de|Einkommen}}, {{m|de|Einkunft|t=income, earnings, competence}}, {{cog|da|indkomst|t=income}}, {{cog|sv|inkomst|t=income}}, {{cog|is|innkváma|t=income}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɪnˌkʌm/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-income.ogg|a=US}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# [[money|Money]] one [[earn]]s by [[work]]ing or by [[capitalise|capitalising]] on the work of others.
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=23|passage=The struggle with ways and means had recommenced, more difficult now a hundredfold than it had been before, because of their increasing needs. Their '''income''' disappeared as a little rivulet that is swallowed by the thirsty ground.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=Dec 4 2010|author=w:Evan Thomas|title=Why It’s Time to Worry|titleurl=http://www.newsweek.com/2010/12/04/the-deepest-dangers-facing-the-united-states.html|journal=Newsweek|accessdate=16 June 2013
|passage=In 1970 the richest 1 percent made 9 percent of the nation’s '''income'''; now that top slice makes closer to 25 percent.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261015125729/https://www.newsweek.com/deepest-dangers-facing-united-states-68883|archivedate=15 October 2026}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-07|author=w:Joseph Stiglitz| volume=188| issue=26| page=19| magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly| title=[http://www.guardian.co.uk/commentisfree/2013/may/27/globalisation-is-about-taxes-too Globalisation is about taxes too]| passage=It is the starving of the public sector which has been pivotal in America no longer being the land of opportunity – with a child's life prospects more dependent on the '''income''' and education of its parents than in other advanced countries.}}
# {{lb|en|business|commerce}} Money coming in to a [[fund]], [[account]], or [[policy]].
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A coming in; [[arrival]]; [[entrance]]; [[introduction]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1667|author={{w|George Rust (bishop)|George Rust}}|title=A Funeral Sermon, preached at the obsequies of {{...}} Jeremy Lord Bishop of Down
|passage=more abundant '''incomes''' of light and strength from God}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Lucrece|passage=Pain payes the income of ech precious thing,}}
# {{lb|en|archaic|or|dialectal|Scotland}} A [[newcomer]] or arrival; an [[incomer]].
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} An [[entrance]]-[[fee]].
# {{lb|en|archaic}} A coming in as by [[influx]] or [[inspiration]], hence, an inspired [[quality]] or [[characteristic]], as [[courage]] or [[zeal]]; an inflowing [[principle]].
#* {{RQ:Homer Chapman Iliads|year=1843|passage=I would then make in indeed and steep / My '''income''' in their bloods.}}
# {{lb|en|UK|_|dialectal|Scotland}} A [[disease]] or [[ailment]] without known or apparent cause, as distinguished from one induced by accident or contagion; an [[oncome]].
# That which is taken into the body as food; the [[ingesta]]; sometimes restricted to the nutritive, or digestible, portion of the food.
